notes: Account summary: mid-stage evaluation for Dedicated capacity. Heavy focus on predictable throughput and strict latency SLOs for customer-facing chat and personalization APIs.

Primary contact: Jordan Patel (Head of ML Infra) + Megan Ortiz (Procurement). Jordan: 'cannot tolerate noisy neighbors — must have strict isolation or preemption', asked for architecture diagram showing tenant lanes.

Use-case details: support agent (low latency chat) + reranking for realtime recommendations. Peak expected QPS: 200-300 req/s with burst to 600 for short windows. Typical payloads: 512-1024 tokens, average response token length ~120.
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 < 150ms for chat generation; throughput baseline 250 req/s sustained. Reranking latency SLO p95 < 70ms.

Reserved GPU planning: customer prefers H100 class for low-latency workloads. Initial ask: reserve 8 dedicated GPUs, burst pool of 4 GPUs. Want guidance on slot sizing and headroom for 99th percentile tails.

SLA negotiation points: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool, financial credits for p99 latency misses, SLO definitions for degraded performance, clear escalation path. Legal asked to see example MSA and SLA language.

Traffic shaping request: per-route quotas + priority lanes. Requirements: ability to assign high-priority lane to "support-chat" route (guaranteed qps and token-rate), medium-priority to "personalization" (elastic), low-priority to batch reranks. Must support weighted fair-share and emergency preemption.

Tenant isolation preferences: strict cgroup-like isolation at GPU scheduler level, per-tenant KV cache partitions, separate KV cache quotas to avoid eviction storms across tenants. Also asked for host-level limits (CPU/memory) for sidecar components.

Noisy-neighbor controls discussed: per-route token-throttles, per-tenant concurrency caps, detect-and-throttle heuristics (token burn-rate) + automated fallback routing to smaller model variant if tail lat spikes. Want a 'circuit-breaker' that drops to best-effort lane before customer-visible errors.

Routing & fallback: 'smart routing' policy needed — route based on latency budget then cost tier; support auto-fallback to 8-bit quantized variant when Dedicated is saturated. Jordan asked for failure-mode docs.

Observability/telemetry: need token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, GPU utilization heatmaps, and KV cache miss/eviction metrics (retention window 90 days). Audit logs for all admin changes.

POC plan agreed: 2-week soak on a Dedicated pool -> verify throughput and p99 lat with synthetic + real traffic; step 1: baseline run without priority lanes; step 2: enable priority lanes and run mixed traffic; step 3: simulate noisy neighbor by injecting high-concurrency client to validate throttles and preemption.

Technical Qs outstanding: how are priority lanes implemented (namespace vs cgroup vs scheduler token-bucket)? how are per-route quotas enforced inside continuous batching runtime? can KV cache partitions be reserved per-tenant?

Integration notes: require SSO/SAML SAML metadata for admin access, KMS integration for model keys, SOC2/ISO27001 paperwork in drive link. Prod network must allow VPC peering with private control plane.

Procurement notes: draft SOW needs to reflect reserved GPU counts, SLA latency credits, and a clause for traffic-shaping behavior during maintenance windows. Megan expects legal response within 3 weeks.
Quotes from meetings: 'We need predictable tail lat — everything else is secondary.' — Jordan P. ; 'If we can't guarantee p99 under load, we won't put customer-facing chat on this' — Megan O.

Next steps logged: prepare POC config (GPU counts, priority lane policies), send SOW draft, schedule kickoff for POC (target 2025-02-18), security to review KMS doc. AE to confirm pricing for reserved 8+4 GPU config.

Internal AE/SE notes: recommend 10% headroom above predicted peak, enable two priority lanes (high/medium) and one best-effort; propose autoscale burst policy with max burst of 50% additional GPUs for 10min windows. Prepare test harness for noisy neighbor injection (INF-1302).
